description: Mechanism-level cards distilled from the GPU DB literature journal. Papers are evidence; mechanisms are the units that can be combined into architecture.

mechanisms.name: WAL-before-visibility boundary
mechanisms.summary: Durable commit evidence must exist before SQL-visible state or route eligibility advances.
risks: throughput pressure if every internal metadata write is placed on the commit-critical path
mechanisms.benchmark: Crash-injected commit and route-publication matrix proving no visible generation lacks durable WAL evidence.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Durability before SQL-visible publication is a non-negotiable correctness invariant, and many downstream route/root/fallback mechanisms require it.

mechanisms.name: Immutable route roots
mechanisms.summary: Publish route, catalog, layout, residency, and visibility metadata as immutable bodies plus compact root generations.
risks: retired descriptor buildup under long readers
mechanisms.benchmark: Route-root publish benchmark comparing full rewrite, in-place mutation, and immutable-body/root-swap under crash injection.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Compact immutable generations give the architecture a shared publication contract for routes, catalogs, residency, and visibility.

mechanisms.name: Dependency witnesses
mechanisms.summary: Represent delayed internal publication as explicit dependency chains that must fence before external eligibility.
risks: unbounded chains if witnesses are never collapsed
mechanisms.benchmark: Async body-persist simulator that proves readers see only fenced roots while measuring ordered flush reduction.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Async publication needs explicit dependency proof, but the witness representation should be prototyped before fixing hot-path shape.

mechanisms.name: Semantic crash oracle
mechanisms.summary: Test recovery by semantic states and externally visible outcomes rather than by exhaustively enumerating all crash points.
risks: oracle blindness if state model omits a real durable dependency
mechanisms.benchmark: Crash-state generator for WAL, route roots, catalog roots, and residency manifests.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Crash-state validation is required to prove WAL, route-root, catalog, and residency publication boundaries before optimized paths are trusted.

mechanisms.name: Isolation trace oracle
mechanisms.summary: Validate every observed read against allowed snapshot intervals, fallback routes, and write-publication claims.
risks: false confidence if trace instrumentation omits route or generation metadata
mechanisms.benchmark: CPU-only, GPU-retained, split CPU/GPU, and fallback MVCC trace oracle.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Fallback and retained-snapshot routes need continuous external validation that returned versions match the declared isolation contract.

mechanisms.name: Retained GPU snapshots
mechanisms.summary: Keep hot read generations resident on GPU and route matching reads directly when freshness and residency prove valid.
risks: stale reads, HBM pressure, long-reader version retention
mechanisms.benchmark: Same-shape retained lookup benchmark under refresh lag, write churn, and fallback pressure.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Resident read generations are central to the GPU value proposition, but freshness, HBM pressure, and version retention need prototype evidence.

mechanisms.name: Snapshot frontier vectors
mechanisms.summary: Use compact scalar generations on hot paths and vector/frontier state only where cross-owner snapshot proof is required.
risks: vector metadata can dominate the hot path if not collapsed aggressively
mechanisms.benchmark: Vector-scalar visibility simulator across owners with retained snapshot admission and fallback.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Cross-owner visibility proof is required for retained snapshots, while the scalar/vector split needs implementation evidence.

mechanisms.name: MVCC garbage-collection frontiers
mechanisms.summary: Reclaim old versions by exact active snapshot generations and bounded multiversion collection rather than periodic blind cleanup.
source_papers: Scalable Garbage Collection for In-Memory MVCC
Practically and Theoretically Efficient GC for Multiversioning
risks: GC stalls or memory blowup under retained GPU snapshots
mechanisms.benchmark: Long-reader and hot-write MVCC retention benchmark with exact frontier pruning.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Exact active-reader frontiers are needed to bound old versions, but retention behavior under GPU snapshots must be measured.

mechanisms.name: Bounded descriptor reclamation
mechanisms.summary: Retire route, catalog, and plan descriptors through bounded hazard/era/epoch-style protection.
risks: complex helpers may not justify themselves unless descriptor churn is high
mechanisms.benchmark: Route-descriptor churn benchmark with long readers, stalled sessions, and bounded retired bytes.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Immutable publication requires safe descriptor lifetime, while the specific hazard/era/epoch strategy should follow churn measurements.

mechanisms.name: Stable handle indirection
mechanisms.summary: Separate logical row/route identity from movable physical placement through handles, forwarding records, or page tables.
risks: extra lookup cost on latency-critical point reads
mechanisms.benchmark: Handle-table lookup and movement benchmark across HBM, DRAM, and NVMe-resident fragments.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Tier movement and compaction need stable identity, but lookup overhead must be measured before the handle shape is fixed.

mechanisms.name: Vector-credit admission
mechanisms.summary: Admit work using per-boundary credits for requests, bytes, pinned buffers, GPU streams, WAL slots, and response capacity.
risks: too many credit dimensions can make routing brittle
mechanisms.benchmark: 1M logical-session simulator with vector credits and standing-queue telemetry.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Route choice must expose bounded resource budgets up front so GPU, CPU, WAL, buffer, and response queues cannot hide overload.

mechanisms.name: Effective session counting
mechanisms.summary: Count only sessions with ready work or blocked responses as active flows; idle logical sessions consume minimal hot-path capacity.
risks: wake storms when many idle sessions become active together
mechanisms.benchmark: Fan-in activation simulator comparing logical sessions, active flows, and hot-path memory.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Large logical-session counts are a target workload, but active-flow accounting needs a simulator before adoption as a fixed runtime rule.

mechanisms.name: Owner-ring bundling
mechanisms.summary: Drain bounded bundles from owner rings and record why selected or skipped work moved forward.
risks: bundle scoring can become hidden scheduler complexity
mechanisms.benchmark: Owner-drain benchmark comparing FIFO, bundle packing, and troublesome-first selection.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Owner-local bounded drains are promising for low-allocation scheduling, with selection policy and skip telemetry still needing proof.

mechanisms.name: Resource-DAG scheduling
mechanisms.summary: Represent query, refresh, write, transfer, kernel, and response work as small dependency DAGs over scarce resources.
risks: estimation errors can make p99 worse than FIFO
mechanisms.benchmark: Route-DAG simulator over refresh, H2D, kernel, D2H, and response fragments.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: DAG scheduling could improve scarce-resource packing, but estimation errors can hurt p99 and must be benchmarked against simpler queues.

mechanisms.name: Deficit fairness
mechanisms.summary: Allow short-term throughput-favorable scheduling while tracking deficits so interactive or tenant classes do not starve.
risks: fairness accounting can fight route packing if classes are too fine-grained
mechanisms.benchmark: Mixed class retained-read benchmark with throughput, p99, and deficit bound gates.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Fairness counters are needed to bound batching and DAG scheduling bias, but policy constants should come from mixed-class measurements.

mechanisms.name: Same-shape micro-batching
mechanisms.summary: Batch repeated prepared route shapes by snapshot generation, partition, and result shape before GPU execution.
risks: batch waiting can hurt single-query latency
mechanisms.benchmark: Prepared point lookup and aggregate micro-batch curves over p50, p99, and GPU occupancy.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Repeated route shapes are a core GPU execution opportunity, while batch limits need latency and occupancy curves before adoption.

mechanisms.name: GPU OLTP conflict ordering
mechanisms.summary: Preprocess large transaction batches to detect conflicts and execute compatible work on GPU.
requires: known access sets or conservative conflict model
risks: not suitable for arbitrary low-latency OLTP without bounded batch delay
mechanisms.benchmark: YCSB/TPC-C style hot-key batch benchmark comparing CPU OCC, owner serialization, and GPU conflict ordering.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: GPU conflict preprocessing is useful only for specific hot-key batch regimes and must compete with CPU OCC and owner serialization.

mechanisms.name: Deterministic hot-write templates
mechanisms.summary: Use predictable per-object queues or deterministic templates for highly contended writes to avoid abort/retry amplification.
risks: templates can over-specialize and reduce general SQL flexibility
mechanisms.benchmark: Zipfian hot-key simulator comparing retry, ordered locking, owner serialization, and deterministic queue positions.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Hot-write templates may beat abort/retry loops for narrow key shapes, but they should remain benchmark-gated until workload fit is proven.

mechanisms.name: CPU fallback policy
mechanisms.summary: Route stale, unsupported, over-budget, or low-cardinality work to CPU without violating visibility or response guarantees.
risks: fallback can hide GPU readiness gaps if not measured
mechanisms.benchmark: Split CPU/GPU route benchmark with fallback reasons and isolation trace validation.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Every accelerated route needs an explicit safe fallback reason so correctness and latency budgets survive stale residency or resource pressure.

mechanisms.name: HTAP freshness router
mechanisms.summary: Route reads by freshness requirement, snapshot availability, wait budget, and acceleration benefit.
risks: planner can silently choose stale or expensive routes without witness metadata
mechanisms.benchmark: Freshness router benchmark over read-committed, bounded-staleness, and exact-snapshot routes.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Freshness-aware routing is fundamental to retained reads, but exact wait, refresh, and fallback thresholds need prototype feedback.

mechanisms.name: Cost-based route optimizer
mechanisms.summary: Choose CPU, GPU, retained snapshot, refresh, transfer, or fallback routes from measured cost and cardinality signals.
risks: bad estimates can violate latency targets even if correctness holds
mechanisms.benchmark: Route-choice benchmark over point, range, join, retained, and cold-tier queries.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: The system needs deterministic route choice over CPU, GPU, retained, refresh, and cold paths before learning or advanced placement can matter.

mechanisms.name: Learned optimizer advisor
mechanisms.summary: Use ML or adaptive learning to suggest route, knob, or placement decisions while keeping correctness outside the model.
risks: model drift and opaque decisions in correctness-sensitive paths
mechanisms.benchmark: Advisor-vs-baseline route selection with guardrail rejections and p99/regret tracking.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Learned route advice should wait until deterministic route telemetry, guardrails, and baseline costs are stable.

mechanisms.name: Multi-tier placement policy
mechanisms.summary: Place fragments across HBM, DRAM, compressed host memory, NVMe, object storage, and future CXL/NVM by measured reuse and movement cost.
risks: movement can break route stability without handles and generations
mechanisms.benchmark: Tier-placement simulator measuring HBM hit rate, movement latency, p99, and write amplification.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: HBM/DRAM/NVMe placement is necessary for capacity, but movement costs and hit-rate targets need simulator and prototype data.

mechanisms.name: Log-structured warm tier
mechanisms.summary: Treat future DRAM/NVM/CXL warm metadata and fragments as append/log-structured homes with rebuildable volatile indexes.
risks: write amplification and recovery scan time if logs are not bounded
mechanisms.benchmark: Warm-tier manifest benchmark comparing append-map rebuild, in-place metadata, and root publication.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: A rebuildable warm tier may simplify recovery, but append-map, root-publication, and in-place metadata variants need direct comparison.

mechanisms.name: DB-owned cold objects
mechanisms.summary: Manage cold blobs, segments, and object-store files with database-owned layout, aging, and metadata rather than generic filesystem assumptions.
risks: scope creep into a full filesystem if interfaces are not narrow
mechanisms.benchmark: Cold-object read/write/compaction benchmark with object manifest crash recovery.
mechanisms.decision_rationale: Cold object manifests should be DB-owned to preserve recovery and routing semantics, with compaction and backup boundaries still to prove.
